chunks: From him, from Abdullah ibn Bahru, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I asked him about a man who buys gold with silver, one unit for two units. He said, 'There is no objection to it, hand to hand.'

key_terms.مِثْلًا بِمِثْلَيْنِ: one unit for two units (inequality in measure)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to buy gold with silver at a different weight ratio?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies that unequal exchange between gold and silver is permissible provided it is 'hand to hand' (yadan bi-yadin), distinguishing it from the prohibition of *riba al-fadl* which applies when the measure differs but the hand-to-hand condition is not met. It reflects the Shia juristic consensus that gold and silver are distinct commodities with their own specific measures, allowing for quantity disparity as long as the transaction is immediate. This ruling underscores the practical application of avoiding usury in commercial exchanges within Islamic finance.
